'''''Azara serrata''''', the '''saw-toothed azara''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Salicaceae]].<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:111475-1 |title= Azara serrata Ruiz & Pav. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=January 26, 2025}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/K5JR |title= Azara serrata Ruiz & Pav. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=January 26, 2025}}</ref> It is endemic to Chile. It is an [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] growing to {{convert|4 |m|ft|abbr=on}}, with glossy serrated leaves and clusters of scented yellow flowers in summer. In [[temperateness|temperate]] regions it requires a sheltered position.<ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=1-4053-3296-4|page=1136}}</ref>

Two varieties are accepted:<ref name=POWO/>
*[[Azara serrata var. fernandeziana|''Azara serrata'' var. ''fernandeziana'']] {{small|(Gay) Reiche}} – Juan Fernández Islands
*[[Azara serrata var. serrata|''Azara serrata'' var. ''serrata'']] – central and southern Chile

This species has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Azara serrata''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/1937/Azara-serrata/Details | access-date=15 April 2020}}</ref>
